title: Closing a skin wound
summary: Close a 5 cm forearm laceration under local anaesthetic with interrupted sutures.

steps.title: Introduce yourself and check identity
steps.prompt: Hello… are you the doctor doing my operation?

choices.text: Hello, I'm one of the surgical team. Can you tell me your full name and date of birth?
Yes. Let's get started straight away.
choices.feedback: Introduce yourself and confirm identity first.

steps.hint: Name, role, then two identifiers from the patient, checked against the wristband.

steps.title: Pick up the skin preparation
steps.hint: Alcoholic chlorhexidine, applied from the incision site outwards.

steps.title: Prepare the skin over the laceration
steps.hint: Centre outwards, wider than the incision; let it dry fully before drapes and diathermy (it is flammable).

steps.title: Draw up local anaesthetic
steps.hint: 1 % lidocaine; check the maximum safe dose for the patient's weight first.

steps.title: Safe dose
steps.prompt: The patient weighs 70 kg. What is the maximum dose of plain 1 % lidocaine?

choices.feedback: That is the dose with adrenaline (7 mg/kg).
That exceeds the safe dose: risk of toxicity.

steps.hint: 3 mg/kg plain, 7 mg/kg with adrenaline; 1 % = 10 mg per ml.

steps.title: Infiltrate the wound edges
steps.hint: Aspirate before injecting; wait for the anaesthetic to work.

steps.title: Choose the suture
steps.prompt: Which suture suits skin on the forearm?

choices.text: 4-0 non-absorbable monofilament on a cutting needle
choices.feedback: Correct: fine, low reactivity, cutting needle for dermis.

choices.text: 1 braided absorbable on a round-bodied needle
choices.feedback: Too thick, and round needles are for soft tissue.
Too fine and the wrong needle for skin.

steps.title: Load the needle
steps.hint: Grip the needle two thirds from the point, in the tip of the needle holder.

steps.title: Take the toothed forceps
steps.hint: Toothed forceps for skin; hold them like a pen.

steps.title: Place the first suture in the middle of the wound
steps.hint: Enter at 90°, bites as far from the edge as the skin is thick, evert the edges.

steps.title: Halve the remaining gaps with interrupted sutures, about 5 mm apart
steps.hint: Instrument ties, three throws, knots to one side.

steps.title: Cut the ends
steps.hint: Leave 5 mm tails so they can be removed.

steps.title: Aftercare
steps.prompt: When should forearm sutures usually come out?

choices.feedback: Too early: the wound would open.
Too late: suture marks and infection.
